summary: This Google Patents page describes German patent DE10008182A1 (granted 2004, filed 2000-02-23 by GKN Automotive GmbH) for a wheel driving and mounting unit for a motor vehicle. The unit combines a wheel carrier, a wheel hub, a rolling bearing and a constant velocity (CV) joint whose detachable outer section meshes with the hub, with a circlip holding the teeth axially. The invention allows the CV joint to be assembled and disassembled non-destructively, via a breakout (gap) in the wheel carrier's annular part, without removing the wheel, hub or carrier from the vehicle. The text includes prior art (WO 99/13232, DE 197 00 313 A1, DE 197 51 855 C1) and figure descriptions; the Google boilerplate (classifications, legal status, links) is largely navigational.
one_line: German patent DE10008182A1 for a wheel hub and CV joint unit that allows non-destructive removal of the drive shaft via a circlip and wheel-carrier breakout.
key_facts: Publication number DE10008182A1 was filed on 2000-02-23 by GKN Automotive GmbH and published on 2001-09-13.
The patent was granted on 2004-03-18 under the publication DE10008182B4.
The listed inventors are Werner Krude and Heinzwilli Fuchs.
The current assignee is listed as GKN Driveline International GmbH.
The wheel driving and mounting component includes a CV joint (71) whose joint outer section (72) can be attached to the wheel hub (41).
The joint between the wheel hub and the joint outer section is in the form of meshing teeth.
A gap or boring (27) in the annular piece (15) of the wheel support takes a circlip.
The stated object is to make assembly and disassembly of the constant velocity joint easier and allow shaft exchange on the motor vehicle.
The breakout in the wheel carrier lets a pliers tool reach the circlip through the recess without removing the wheel, wheel hub or wheel carrier.
The description states that disassembly without destroying the circlip was not possible in the prior art WO 99/13232.
DE 197 00 313 A1 uses a snap-ring type circlip that is crushed during forcible axial removal, possibly damaging the gears.
The breakout is described as essentially U-shaped in axial view to rule out peak loads and ensure a harmonious force course.
The wheel carrier's screw connections on both sides of the breakout to the bearing outer ring compensate for the material reduction.
The legal status is listed as Expired - Fee Related, with anticipated expiration on 2020-02-24.
Corresponding applications were filed for US10/204,835, JP2001561923A, PCT/EP2000/012709 and AU2001230115A1.
